discovery: Discovery of magnetic skyrmions in chiral magnets and their emergent electromagnetism

nominees.name: Yoshinori Tokura
nominees.affiliation: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and University of Tokyo, Japan

subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological magnetism, strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: In 2009 Pfleiderer, Rosch and co-workers found by neutron scattering a lattice of topological spin textures, skyrmions, in the chiral magnet MnSi. In 2010 Tokura's group imaged individual skyrmions and skyrmion crystals in real space by Lorentz electron microscopy, later down to room temperature and in thin films. Together they showed that skyrmions are stable particle-like objects protected by topology. Their Berry phase acts on conduction electrons as an emergent magnetic field, producing the topological Hall effect, and their motion generates an emergent electric field. They can be driven by currents a million times weaker than those needed to move domain walls. This work established topology in real space as an organizing principle of magnetism, has since been extended to many materials and to antiskyrmions and hopfions, and opened a route to low-power spintronic memory and logic devices.
